newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Senate panel advances electronic tolls bill.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Senate panel advances electronic tolls bill.

text.p: The New Jersey Senate's Budget and Appropriations Committee Monday approved legislation allowing for electronic toll collection on New Jersey's main highways.

"This legislation is long overdue," said Sen. William Haines, R-Mt. Laurel, a sponsor of the legislation. "Electronic toll collection has been proven effective in reducing congestion and speeding the flow of traffic."

Haines said electronic tolls, which use electronic readers to permit motorists to pay their tolls without stopping at booths, would cut the number of personnel needed at the state's major authorities.
If approved, electronic tolls would be implemented on the Garden State Parkway, the Turnpike, and the Atlantic City Expressway next year.
The bills allowing electronic toll implementation are now headed to the full Senate for a vote.
